en: National hero Jose Rizal was a polyglot who could speak and write in twenty-two different languages, including Arabic, Hebrew, and Sanskrit.
The Philippine Senate has exactly twenty-four members elected at large, meaning every single voter in the country casts a ballot for the exact same candidates.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, is the longest and has the largest wing surface of any eagle in the world.
The first Philippine flag was hand-sewn in Hong Kong by Marcela Agoncillo, her daughter Lorenza, and Delfina Herbosa de Natividad, Jose Rizal's niece.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, the first female student at Harvard Medical School, invented a makeshift bamboo incubator to help premature babies in rural areas.
The ancient pre-colonial Filipino writing system called Baybayin contains only seventeen characters, specifically three vowels and fourteen consonants.
The T'boli indigenous people of South Cotabato weave their sacred t'nalak cloth from abaca fibers based on patterns they see in their dreams.
Juan Luna’s massive Spoliarium painting is so huge that it measures over seven meters wide and took two years of continuous work to finish.
The Sangguniang Kabataan is a unique local government body in the Philippines specifically led by elected youth officials aged fifteen to seventeen.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, is known as the mother of all Philippine festivals and inspired the creation of Sinulog and Dinagyang.
During the 1898 independence proclamation in Kawit, Cavite, the Philippine national anthem was played publicly for the very first time by a local band.
The Philippine Supreme Court requires its fifteen justices to be at least forty years old and have fifteen years of legal experience before serving.
